blocks.text: All chemical reactions involve the breaking of bonds in the reactant molecules before new bonds form, which can happen only if the reactant molecules collide with enough energy to overcome an energy barrier.

blocks.title: Energy of activation
blocks.text: The minimum amount of energy required by the reactant molecules just to cross the energy barrier is the energy of activation, Ea.

blocks.alt: Two graphs of enthalpy against progress of reaction. On the left a red curve rises from the reactants over a hump and falls to products lower down, with Ea marked to the top of the hump and a downward arrow for delta H. On the right a blue curve rises over a larger hump to products higher than the reactants, with an upward delta H arrow.
blocks.caption: Energy profile diagrams of an exothermic and an endothermic reaction showing delta H and Ea (original diagram after Figures 6.1 and 6.2).
blocks.long_description: In both diagrams the reactants must first climb to the top of the barrier, which takes the activation energy Ea, before they can fall to the products. In the exothermic case the products lie below the reactants, so delta H is negative and heat is released; in the endothermic case the products lie above the reactants, so delta H is positive and heat is absorbed, and the barrier is larger than delta H. The height of the hump is Ea and the difference between the two levels is delta H.
